Search a constrained set of CPUE models

Source: R/model-search.R
search_cpue.Rd

A bounded, buildmer-style search using each backend's native fitter and information criteria. The default is a preflight report: fitting requires the explicit argument refit = TRUE.

Usage

search_cpue(
  model,
  year = NULL,
  scope = NULL,
  include = NULL,
  optional = NULL,
  direction = c("order", "backward"),
  criterion = "auto",
  max_models = 50,
  refit = FALSE,
  data = NULL,
  component = NULL,
  keep_fits = "best",
  refit_args = list(),
  seed = NULL,
  blocks = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'influ_search'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'influ_search'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'influ_search'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

model

One fitted GLM, mgcv GAM, glmmTMB, lme4, brms, sdmTMB, or tinyVAST model. Each search uses one backend and one family/link.

year

Optional name of the annual variable. Otherwise the annual variable is detected using the same conventions as other CPUE interfaces.

scope

Optional upper formula, or a list with lower and upper formulas. The fitted formula is the default upper scope. Required terms are retained even when omitted from a supplied scope.

include

Additional terms to retain, as a one-sided formula or character vector. For annual interaction coding, explicitly include the base annual block, for example ~ fyear:season.

optional

Optional formula or character vector naming the only terms to search. Other terms remain protected. This can explicitly nominate non-essential random effects; annual base terms and offsets cannot be released. Without this argument, ordinary covariates are optional, while random effects and multidimensional smooths are protected.

direction

"forward", "backward", "both", or c("order", "backward"). The latter builds an admissible maximal model by adding converged blocks to the protected core, then prunes it. Ordering can add terms even when the criterion increases. Other moves must improve the criterion by more than a numerical tolerance of 1e-6.

criterion

"auto", "AIC", "BIC", "cAIC", or "LOOIC" (also "loo"). Automatic selection uses AIC for frequentist backends and LOOIC for brms. Native cAIC is only available for supported backends; no replacement mixed-model penalty is invented.

max_models

Positive integer limit on distinct evaluated candidate specifications, including a reused original fit. Failed candidates count.

refit

Logical; FALSE reports the constraints and fitting plan without optimisation, MCMC, or criterion calculation.

data

Optional original raw data, required when the saved call cannot recover them. Fitted rows, responses, weights, and offsets are checked.

component

For a joint sdmTMB delta model, explicitly select "occurrence" or "positive"; the other component stays fixed.

keep_fits

"best" (default), "all", or "none". Native fit objects can be large; candidate tables and paths are always compact.

refit_args

Named list of native execution controls. Structural changes to families, data, offsets, priors, meshes, or process definitions are rejected. For lme4 negative-binomial models, explicitly state reestimate_nb = TRUE or FALSE.

seed

Optional non-negative integer. Evaluation seeds are recorded; a reused fit retains its original draws. The caller's random-number state is restored on success or failure.

blocks

Optional named list of disjoint term groups, moved together. Members use term labels, not coefficient names.

x, object

An `influ_search` object.

...

Reserved for additional method arguments.

row.names

Optional row names for the data-frame method. Its generic `optional` argument is reserved and does not change the retained table.

Value

An influ_search object with terms, candidates, path, metadata, and the retained best_model (unless keep_fits = "none"). selected_model() retrieves the recommended native fit. Printing, summaries, and plotting use stored results without new fits or simulations.

Details

Year, response definition, offsets, weights, and essential random/spatial structure are fixed specifications, not fixed numerical estimates. Estimated coefficients, variance/dispersion parameters, and latent effects are re-estimated in each candidate, except parameters deliberately fixed in the original native specification. Formula terms are atomic, and interaction dependencies present in the upper scope are respected. New main effects are not invented for intentional interaction-only annual coding.

Gaussian mixed models fitted by REML are refitted using ML for searching fixed effects; this conversion is recorded. mgcv's native AIC is not its REML smoothing objective. Priors/penalties that invalidate ordinary maximum-likelihood ranking, missing convergence evidence, unreliable brms LOO estimates, and incompatible observations/likelihood targets make a candidate ineligible, rather than silently switching criteria.

Every distinct specification is evaluated at most once. The recommendation is the best eligible evaluated model, not a guaranteed global optimum. Search stopping, warnings, singular fits, and failed fits remain visible. There is no production refitting, search-driven residual simulation, model averaging, or automatic spatial-process selection. Advanced nonlinear or distributional formulas that cannot safely retain auxiliary specifications fail explicitly. Positional parameter maps are not automatically remapped as terms change: explicitly mapped TMB models require separately specified candidates instead. Stored sdmTMB latent-process formulas and native trial counts are retained, rather than re-evaluated from changed call variables. Use check_cpue() on the shortlist separately: residual p-values are not term-removal rules. Post-selection intervals remain conditional on the chosen model and do not include selection uncertainty. Compact retention limits stored results, not native fitting, LOO, or Hessian workspace. In particular, brms criterion calculations can still require substantial temporary memory.

References

Voeten (2020). buildmer: Stepwise elimination and term ordering for mixed models. https://cran.r-project.org/package=buildmer.

See also

table_criterion(), check_cpue(), influ_steps(), cpue_index()

Examples

set.seed(12)
d <- data.frame(year = factor(rep(2020:2023, each = 15)), x = rnorm(60))
d$response <- rpois(60, exp(1 + 0.5 * d$x))
fit <- glm(response ~ year + x, data = d, family = poisson())
search_cpue(fit, year = "year") # preflight only
#> <influ_search> glm / AIC
#>   Mode: preflight only
#>   Protected terms: 1
#>   Evaluated candidates: 0
#>   Stop: preflight_only
result <- search_cpue(fit, year = "year", direction = "backward", refit = TRUE)
result$candidates[c("candidate", "formula", "score", "status")]
#>   candidate                 formula    score   status
#> 1         1 response ~ (year) + (x) 219.6487 eligible
#> 2         2       response ~ (year) 262.7810 eligible
selected_model(result)
#> 
#> Call:  glm(formula = response ~ year + x, family = poisson(), data = d)
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#> (Intercept)     year2021     year2022     year2023            x  
#>     1.24374     -0.04885     -0.47464     -0.21159      0.55398  
#> 
#> Degrees of Freedom: 59 Total (i.e. Null);  55 Residual
#> Null Deviance:	    100.6 
#> Residual Deviance: 47.38 	AIC: 219.6
